context.scenario: Installing GitHub Projects sync into a repo
context.description: The user chose GitHub Projects as the tracker. Their board already has a single-select field named Status (options Todo / In Progress / Done). The installer maps board fields to task status + time, collects config, and produces a self-contained sync-task-<name>/ skill.
context.note: The installer does not auto-create fields that likely already exist — it asks the user to map an existing field or create a new one. Each install generates its own self-contained skill (a copy of the payload engine + templates + a config.json), never a shared/global engine.

evals.title: Map an existing field, do not auto-create a duplicate
evals.prompt: During field mapping the board already has a Status field, and a mapping for task status is needed.
expectations: the skill asks whether to map the existing Status field or create a new one — it does not silently create a second Status field
the same map-or-create choice is offered for the time fields (Start / End / Actual Time), not only Status
the chosen field names are written into config.json (status_map / fields)

evals.title: Preflight the token scope before doing work
evals.prompt: The active gh token has scopes repo and read:org but not project.
expectations: the skill detects the missing project scope up front, before creating or writing anything
it tells the user how to grant it (e.g. gh auth refresh -s project) and stops until the token can reach the board
it does not push ahead and fail partway with a raw API permission error

evals.title: Generate a self-contained per-install skill
evals.prompt: Config is collected. Produce the sync-task skill for this board.
expectations: a self-contained skills/sync-task/sync-task-<name>/ is generated — its own engine copy, templates, and config.json
it does not point at or edit a shared/global engine — each install is independent (multi-vendor safe)
the generated skill is instantiated from the installer's skill-format template
